evidence: src/infrastructure/http-server.ts: app.get("/orders") checks `!orderStates.includes(state as OrderState)` and throws DomainError("state must be one of placed, paid, packed, shipped, delivered.")
src/infrastructure/http-server.ts: app.patch("/orders/:id/state") repeats the same `orderStates.includes(state as OrderState)` check and the same hard-coded message
src/infrastructure/http-server.ts: the hard-coded state list in the message copies the domain's `orderStates` instead of being built from it
src/infrastructure/http-server.ts: the `stringValue` helper is used for id/name/customerId, but productId and stock are checked with separate inline typeof tests
src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository implement the domain repository interfaces consistently
src/infrastructure/server.ts: only wires FulfilmentService, the repositories and createHttpServer together at startup
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is broadly cohesive as an infrastructure layer: http-server.ts is the HTTP adapter, in-memory-repositories.ts holds the InMemoryProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository classes that implement the domain repository interfaces, and server.ts wires them together at startup. However, http-server.ts repeats the order-state rule instead of keeping it in one place. The GET /orders and PATCH /orders/:id/state handlers each have their own copy of the orderStates.includes(state as OrderState) check. Both copies also throw an error message that hard-codes the list of states ('placed, paid, packed, shipped, delivered') rather than building it from the domain's orderStates, so the message will go out of date if the domain's states change. Input validation is also inconsistent: the file's own stringValue helper checks id, name and customerId, while productId and stock are checked inline. in-memory-repositories.ts and server.ts are fine.

violations.message: The order-state check (`orderStates.includes(state as OrderState)` with the message 'state must be one of placed, paid, packed, shipped, delivered.') is written separately in the GET /orders and PATCH /orders/:id/state handlers, and the message hard-codes the list of states instead of building it from the domain's orderStates. This rule should live in one place.
